candidates.phrase: two whole and perfect natures, that is to say, the Godhead and Manhood, were joined
candidates.rationale: Asserts the two natures remain whole and perfect while joined in one person, affirming their union without collapse of distinction.
candidates.chunk_text: The Son, who is the Word of the Father, the very and eternal God, of one substance with the Father, took man's nature in the womb of the blessed Virgin; so that two whole and perfect natures, that is to say, the Godhead and Manhood, were joined together in one person, never to be divided; whereof is one Christ, very God and very Man, who truly suffered, was crucified, dead, and buried, to reconcile his Father to us, and to be a sacrifice, not only for original guilt, but also for actual sins of men.

candidates.rationale: Asserts Christ has two distinct natures held together in union, implying their distinction is preserved rather than collapsed.
candidates.chunk_text: We believe in Jesus Christ, truly God and truly man, in whom the divine and human natures are perfectly and inseparably united. He is the eternal Word made flesh, the only begotten Son of the Father, born of the Virgin Mary by the power of the Holy Spirit. As ministering Servant he lived, suffered and died on the cross. He was buried, rose from the dead and ascended into heaven to be with the Father, from whence he shall return. He is eternal Savior and Mediator, who intercedes for us, and by him all men will be judged.

Q-415-p1-BSR-MW-01-1.source_note: Article II of the Articles of Religion states that Christ's Godhead and Manhood are 'two whole and perfect natures... joined together in one person, never to be divided.'
Q-415-p1-BSR-MW-01-1.scope_caveat: The Articles of Religion and the EUB Confession are constitutionally protected standards of the United Methodist Church. The Global Methodist Church, which separated in 2022, holds the same Articles; its standards are cited here from its 2022 Transitional Book of Doctrines and Discipline, the only edition published on the church's own domain, and the Articles are unchanged in the 2024 edition. The Wesleyan Church holds its own articles, which the registry lists separately.

survivors.locator: Article II — Of the Word, or Son of God, Who Was Made Very Man
survivors.phrase: two whole and perfect natures, that is to say, the Godhead and Manhood, were joined
survivors.rationale: Asserts the two natures remain whole and perfect while joined in one person, affirming their union without collapse of distinction.
survivors.chunk_text: The Son, who is the Word of the Father, the very and eternal God, of one substance with the Father, took man's nature in the womb of the blessed Virgin; so that two whole and perfect natures, that is to say, the Godhead and Manhood, were joined together in one person, never to be divided; whereof is one Christ, very God and very Man, who truly suffered, was crucified, dead, and buried, to reconcile his Father to us, and to be a sacrifice, not only for original guilt, but also for actual sins of men.
survivors.recut_from: two whole and perfect natures, that is to say, the Godhead and Manhood, were joined together

survivors.phrase: the divine and human natures are perfectly and inseparably united
survivors.rationale: Asserts Christ has two distinct natures held together in union, implying their distinction is preserved rather than collapsed.
survivors.chunk_text: We believe in Jesus Christ, truly God and truly man, in whom the divine and human natures are perfectly and inseparably united. He is the eternal Word made flesh, the only begotten Son of the Father, born of the Virgin Mary by the power of the Holy Spirit. As ministering Servant he lived, suffered and died on the cross. He was buried, rose from the dead and ascended into heaven to be with the Father, from whence he shall return. He is eternal Savior and Mediator, who intercedes for us, and by him all men will be judged.
